courses.title: Enterprise Risk Management: Foundations
courses.summary: Build a shared language for risk and learn how to identify, assess and respond to the risks that matter to your objectives.
courses.overview: Most organisations have risk registers; far fewer use risk to make better decisions. This two-day programme gives managers and staff a practical grounding in enterprise risk management (ERM): what it is, why it matters, and how it connects strategy, objectives and day-to-day work. Participants leave able to contribute confidently to their organisation's risk process.
outcomes: Explain ERM and how it links to strategy and objectives
Identify risks using structured techniques
Assess likelihood and impact on a consistent scale
Choose appropriate risk responses and owners
Read and contribute to a useful risk register
Understand roles across the Three Lines Model

courses.title: Enterprise Risk Management: A Practical Approach (Level 2)
courses.summary: Move from theory to practice: embed ERM into planning, decisions and performance with an implementation roadmap and KPIs.
courses.overview: ERM is a journey, not a one-off training event. Building on foundation concepts, this hands-on programme focuses on implementation: aligning existing structures with ERM, running effective risk workshops, defining KPIs and making risk part of everyday management decisions. Participants work on their own organisation's risks throughout.
outcomes: Design a practical ERM implementation roadmap
Facilitate risk workshops that produce useful results
Integrate risk into planning and budgeting
Define KRIs and ERM performance measures
Analyse root causes and interconnected risks
Strengthen risk culture and ownership

modules.title: From framework to practice
topics: Aligning ERM with existing governance structures
Maturity assessment of your current ERM

modules.title: Advanced risk identification
topics: Scenario analysis and stress testing basics

modules.title: Embedding risk in decisions
topics: Risk in strategy, projects and procurement

courses.title: ISO 31000 Risk Management in Practice
courses.summary: Apply the ISO 31000 principles, framework and process to design or strengthen a risk management system that fits your organisation.
courses.overview: ISO 31000 is the world's most widely used risk management standard. This programme walks through its principles, framework and process clause by clause, with case studies and exercises that show how to apply it in public, private and non-profit settings. Note: this is a practical application course, not an ISO certification exam.
outcomes: Explain the ISO 31000 principles, framework and process
Assess an organisation's risk framework against the standard
Apply the risk process from context to monitoring
Integrate risk with ISO 9001, 27001 and other systems
Design risk policies, criteria and registers
Plan improvements to risk management maturity

modules.title: Introduction to ISO 31000
topics: Purpose, scope and structure of the standard

modules.title: The eight principles
topics: Inclusive, dynamic and based on best information
Human and cultural factors; continual improvement

courses.title: COSO Internal Control: Design & Assessment
courses.summary: Use the COSO Internal Control framework's five components and 17 principles to design, document and assess effective controls.
courses.overview: Strong internal control protects assets, reporting and reputation. This programme explains the COSO 2013 Internal Control – Integrated Framework in practical terms and shows how to document processes, map risks to controls and assess whether controls are designed and operating effectively.
outcomes: Explain the five COSO components and 17 principles
Build risk and control matrices
Distinguish preventive, detective, manual and automated controls
Test control design and operating effectiveness
Evaluate and report control deficiencies
Strengthen the control environment

courses.title: Risk-Based Internal Auditing
courses.summary: Plan and deliver audits that focus on the risks that matter, aligned with the Global Internal Audit Standards.
courses.overview: Risk-based auditing directs limited audit resources to the areas of greatest risk and value. This programme covers the full audit cycle — from the audit universe and annual plan to engagement planning, fieldwork, reporting and follow-up — using practical templates and case studies.
audience: External auditors moving into internal audit
outcomes: Build an audit universe and risk-based annual plan
Plan engagements around key risks and objectives
Design effective audit work programmes
Gather sufficient and reliable evidence
Write findings using criteria, condition, cause and effect
Follow up recommendations effectively

courses.title: Leading Audit Engagements: Tools & Techniques
courses.summary: For senior auditors stepping up to lead engagements: coaching teams, challenging evidence and maintaining audit quality.
courses.overview: Audit quality begins before fieldwork. This advanced programme equips senior auditors and audit leads with the tools to plan engagements well, supervise and coach teams, apply professional scepticism and turn exceptions into meaningful findings that management acts on.
audience: Audit supervisors in firms and SACCOs
outcomes: Lead engagement planning and scoping
Use risk and control matrices and walk-throughs effectively
Design efficient test plans with data analytics
Supervise, coach and review working papers
Apply professional scepticism and judgement
Deliver findings that drive action

courses.title: IT Audit & Cyber Risk Essentials
courses.summary: Understand IT general controls, cyber risk and how to audit technology — no programming background required.
courses.overview: Every business process now runs on technology. This programme gives auditors, risk and compliance professionals a working knowledge of IT governance, IT general controls and cyber risk, with practical audit programmes for access, change management, operations and third-party technology services.
outcomes: Explain IT governance and IT general controls
Assess access, change and operations controls
Understand common cyber threats and controls
Review backup, recovery and continuity arrangements
Assess third-party and cloud risks
Plan and report an IT audit

courses.title: Data Analytics for Auditors & Risk Professionals
courses.summary: Use Excel and simple analytics to test whole populations, spot anomalies and build dashboards for audit and risk.
courses.overview: Analysing 100% of transactions finds what sampling misses. This hands-on programme teaches practical analytics in Excel — cleaning data, testing populations, detecting anomalies and building simple dashboards — and introduces continuous monitoring. Participants bring a laptop.
outcomes: Obtain and clean data for analysis
Test full populations with Excel functions and pivots
Detect duplicates, gaps and outliers
Apply Benford's Law and other fraud indicators
Build simple audit and risk dashboards
Design a continuous monitoring approach

courses.title: AI for Business: Value & Governance
courses.summary: Where AI creates value today — and the risks leaders must govern. A practical, non-technical day for decision-makers.
courses.overview: AI tools are already in your organisation, whether planned or not. This one-day programme helps leaders separate hype from value, identify practical use cases, and put sensible governance in place for data privacy, accuracy, bias and accountability.
outcomes: Explain what today's AI can and cannot do
Identify high-value use cases in your organisation
Recognise key AI risks: privacy, accuracy, bias, security
Set out an AI policy and governance approach
Understand data protection obligations
Plan a safe first AI pilot

courses.title: Fraud Risk Management & Investigations
courses.summary: Prevent, detect and respond to fraud — from fraud risk assessment to running a sound investigation.
courses.overview: Fraud is cheaper to prevent than to recover. This programme covers how fraud happens, how to assess fraud risk, which controls deter and detect it, and how to handle allegations and investigations properly so that evidence stands up.
outcomes: Explain the fraud triangle and common schemes
Conduct a fraud risk assessment
Design anti-fraud controls and whistleblowing channels
Spot red flags in data and documents
Plan and run a basic investigation
Handle evidence and interviews properly

courses.title: Business Continuity & Operational Resilience
courses.summary: Keep critical services running through disruption with business impact analysis, continuity plans and tested responses.
courses.overview: Power cuts, cyber attacks, pandemics and supplier failures all test an organisation's resilience. This programme takes participants through business impact analysis, continuity strategies, crisis management and exercising plans, aligned with ISO 22301 principles.
outcomes: Conduct a business impact analysis (BIA)
Set recovery time and point objectives
Develop practical continuity strategies and plans
Set up crisis management and communication
Design and run exercises
Audit and improve continuity arrangements

courses.title: Board Effectiveness & Corporate Governance
courses.summary: Help boards move from compliance to oversight that creates value: roles, committees, risk oversight and board evaluation.
courses.overview: Good governance is more than following a code. This executive workshop helps directors and senior leaders sharpen board roles, strengthen committee oversight of risk and audit, ask better questions of management and evaluate board performance. Strengthen audit and risk committee oversight
Ask effective questions about risk and performance
Apply governance codes in practice
Oversee strategy, culture and ethics
Plan a board evaluation

courses.title: Healthcare Risk Management & Patient Safety
courses.summary: Build a high-reliability hospital: turn risk management into everyday clinical and operational behaviour.
courses.overview: In healthcare, risk management is ultimately about protecting lives. This programme helps hospital leaders and staff move beyond policies and registers to practical risk management: learning from near misses, psychological safety, clinical governance and an integrated view of clinical, operational, technology and financial risk.
audience: Risk, compliance and audit staff in healthcare
outcomes: Apply ERM in a hospital setting
Understand High Reliability Organisation principles
Learn from incidents and near misses
Build psychological safety and reporting culture
Link clinical governance with enterprise risk
Track patient safety risk indicators

courses.title: Budgeting, Forecasting & Management Reporting
courses.summary: Build budgets that drive performance, forecasts you can trust and management reports that support decisions.
courses.overview: Finance teams spend weeks on budgets that are out of date by March. This practical programme covers driver-based budgeting, rolling forecasts, cash flow planning and management reports that busy executives actually use, with Excel templates participants take home.
outcomes: Build driver-based budgets
Use rolling forecasts and scenarios
Plan and monitor cash flow
Analyse variances meaningfully
Design concise management reports and dashboards
Link financial and operational KPIs
